author: Lucy Hodgman
title: Man charged with attempted rape after following woman into Berkeley elevator - NewsBreak
text:
By Lucy Hodgman ,
1 hours ago The woman was able to escape when the elevator reached a floor with another person on it and she called for help, police said. (Berkeley Police Department) A man was charged with attempted rape after he allegedly assaulted a woman in the elevator of her downtown Berkeley apartment building, police said.
Sean Johnson, 40, followed the woman into her building at around 3 p.m. Saturday, the Berkeley Police Department said in a statement. He allegedly cornered her in the elevator, where he exposed himself to the woman and began to grope her, authorities said.
More Information
Sean Johnson, 40, is accused of following a woman into her apartment building and trapping her inside the elevator.
The woman was able to escape when the elevator reached a floor with another person on it and she called for help, police said.
Johnson attempted to hide when officers arrived, police said, but was found in a nearby garage and arrested. On Tuesday, the Alameda County District Attorney’s Office charged him with attempted rape, false imprisonment, burglary, sexual battery and possession of a controlled substance.
Johnson was being held without bail in Santa Rita Jail as of Wednesday evening. He was set to appear in court for arraignment Thursday morning.
Alameda County court records show Johnson has prior felony convictions for second-degree burglary in 2020 and 2014 and first-degree residential burglary in 2007.
